Belchatow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bełchatów, Poland

Demolished. Bełchatów, founded in 1737, was one of 246 towns where Jewish residents faced no settlement restrictions, leading to rapid growth — Jews comprised 11 percent of the population by 1809 and 80 percent by 1864. An independent kehilla was founded in 1820, with its own cemetery and synagogue by 1824. Following the March 1941 ghetto's establishment, the Germans began its liquidation in August 1942, transporting most residents to the Chełmno death camp. This older cemetery, established in the first half of the 19th century in the area known as Kempfinówka, was destroyed by the Germans during WWII, its matzevot used to pave sidewalks and regulate the Rakówka riverbed; current residents of the site are reportedly unaware any Jewish cemetery ever stood there.
